recipes.title: Amritsari Paneer Bhurji
instructions: Crumble fresh paneer with your fingers.
Heat oil or butter in a kadai. Saute chopped onions, green chillies, and ginger until translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes, haldi, red chilli powder, and salt. Cook until mushy and oil separates.
Toss in crumbled paneer, mix gently on medium heat for 2-3 minutes. Garnish with chopped hara dhaniya and serve hot with parathas.

recipes.title: Dhaba Style Kadai Paneer
instructions: Cut paneer, onions, and capsicum into 1-inch square cubes/petals.
Make a rich tomato-onion-ginger puree and cook in a pan with whole spices until thick.
Saute capsicum and onion cubes in a separate pan until slightly charred but crisp.
Combine the gravy with sauteed veggies and paneer cubes. Simmer for 4 minutes and finish with crushed kasuri methi.

recipes.title: Homestyle Matar Paneer
instructions: Boil or thaw green peas. Cut paneer into cubes.
Saute onion-tomato-ginger paste with basic spices (haldi, dhaniya, mirch).
Add peas and 1 cup water; bring gravy to a gentle simmer for 7 minutes.
Slide in paneer cubes and simmer for another 3 minutes. Serve with roti or jeera rice.

recipes.title: Desi Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch fresh spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, then transfer to cold water and blend into a bright green puree.
In a pan, cook finely chopped garlic, onions, and tomatoes until soft.
Add the palak puree and simmer with salt and garam masala for 5 minutes.
Gently stir in paneer cubes and a dollop of fresh cream or butter.

recipes.title: Creamy Dahi Tadka
instructions: Whisk thick curd (dahi) in a bowl with salt until smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee or oil in a tadka pan. Add rai, jeera, chopped garlic, curry leaves, and green chillies.
Add sliced onions and saute till golden brown, followed by a pinch of haldi and kashmiri lal mirch.
Turn off heat and pour the sizzling tadka directly over the whisked curd. Mix and serve immediately with hot rotis.

recipes.title: Traditional Besan Dahi Kadhi
instructions: Whisk sour dahi and besan together with 3 cups water, haldi, and salt until lump-free.
Bring mixture to a boil in a deep vessel on medium flame, stirring continuously so curd does not split.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes until thick and aromatic.
Temper with ghee, rai, jeera, methi seeds, hing, dry red chillies, and curry leaves. Pour over kadhi.

recipes.title: Odia / Kashmiri Dahi Baingan
instructions: Slice brinjal (baingan) into round discs, rub with salt and haldi, and pan-fry in oil until tender.
Whisk dahi with salt and roasted jeera powder in a serving dish.
Arrange the fried brinjal slices inside the yogurt.
Temper with mustard seeds, curry leaves, and hing in hot oil, and pour on top.

recipes.title: Dry Aloo Shimla Mirch
instructions: Cut potatoes and capsicum into matching bite-sized cubes.
Heat oil, crackle jeera and hing, then add potatoes and saute covered until 80% tender.
Add onions, tomatoes, haldi, dhaniya powder, and red chilli powder.
Add capsicum last to keep its crunch. Cook uncovered for 4-5 minutes, finish with amchur (dry mango powder) and coriander.

recipes.title: Halwai-Style Jeera Aloo
instructions: Boil, peel, and dice potatoes into cubes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil or ghee. Add a generous tablespoon of jeera, crushed ginger, and green chillies.
Add potatoes, haldi, salt, and dhaniya powder. Toss on high heat until the edges turn golden and crisp.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice, sprinkle chopped fresh dhaniya, and serve.

recipes.title: Crispy Kurkuri Bhindi Masala
instructions: Wash and thoroughly dry bhindi with a towel before slicing into 1-inch rounds to prevent sliminess.
Heat oil in a wide pan, crackle ajwain and jeera, then saute sliced onions till soft.
Add bhindi and cook on medium flame WITHOUT covering to keep it crisp.
Once cooked, add haldi, dhaniya powder, amchur, and salt. Toss for 2 minutes.

recipes.title: Homestyle Aloo Gobi Matar
instructions: Cut cauliflower into florets and potatoes into wedges.
Shallow fry florets and potatoes in 2 tbsp oil until light golden and set aside.
In same pan, saute chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, and tomatoes with dry masalas.
Add green peas, fried veggies, splash of water, cover and cook on low heat until fork-tender.

recipes.title: Smoky Punjabi Baingan Bharta
instructions: Slit large bharta brinjal, insert garlic cloves, and roast directly on an open gas flame until skin is completely charred.
Let cool, peel off blackened skin, and mash the flesh with a fork.
In a kadai, heat mustard oil and saute onions, green chillies, and ginger until brown.
Add tomatoes and cook until pulpy. Add mashed brinjal, salt, red chilli, and cook for 8-10 minutes on medium heat.

recipes.title: Nutritious Lauki Chana Dal
instructions: Soak chana dal for 20 minutes. Peel and dice bottle gourd (lauki) into chunks.
In a pressure cooker, heat oil or ghee, add jeera, hing, chopped onions, and ginger-garlic.
Add tomatoes, haldi, salt, dal, and lauki with 1.5 cups water.
Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles on medium flame. Mash slightly and temper with ghee and jeera.

recipes.title: Kathiyawadi Sev Tamatar Ki Sabzi
instructions: Finely chop ripe juicy tomatoes.
Heat oil, crackle rai, jeera, and hing. Saute green chillies and ginger.
Add tomatoes, haldi, dhaniya powder, red chilli powder, salt, and a pinch of sugar. Cook until tomatoes are juicy and soft.
Add 1/2 cup water to form a spicy gravy. Just before serving, top generously with ratlami or besan sev and fresh coriander.

recipes.title: Quick Fridge-Clearout Mix Veg
instructions: Chop any combination of veggies you have in the fridge (potatoes, capsicum, peas, carrots, cauliflower).
Saute jeera, onions, and ginger-garlic paste in oil.
Add chopped tomatoes and dry spices until fragrant.
Add all veggies, cover with a lid on low flame, and let cook in their own steam until tender.

recipes.title: Dhaba Style Dal Tadka
instructions: Pressure cook toor dal with water, salt, and haldi for 3 whistles until soft.
In a kadai, saute onions, green chillies, and ginger in ghee.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft; pour boiled dal into the gravy and simmer for 5 minutes.
Top with a sizzling double tadka of ghee, sliced garlic, jeera, hing, and kashmiri chilli.

recipes.title: Spicy South Indian Tomato Rasam
instructions: Crush tomatoes by hand in 2 cups water with salt, haldi, and slit green chillies.
Pound garlic cloves, whole black peppercorns, and jeera in a mortar pestle.
Bring tomato water to a gentle boil with the crushed spice mix for 7 minutes.
Temper with mustard seeds, curry leaves, and hing in ghee. Garnish with lots of hara dhaniya.

recipes.title: Light Yellow Moong Dal Fry
instructions: Wash and boil yellow moong dal with haldi and salt for 10-12 minutes.
Heat ghee in a pan. Add jeera, hing, chopped ginger, and slit chillies.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Pour over the boiled dal, bring to one boil, and finish with fresh coriander.

recipes.title: Mumbai Street Style Anda Bhurji
instructions: Whisk 3-4 eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt.
Heat butter or oil in a pan. Add finely chopped onions and green chillies, sauteing until translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes, haldi, pav bhaji masala or red chilli powder, cooking until tomatoes soften.
Pour whisked eggs into the pan on medium-low flame. Scramble gently until soft and fluffy. Garnish with coriander and serve with buttered pav or rotis.

recipes.title: Tariwali Desi Egg Curry
instructions: Hard boil 4 eggs, peel them, make tiny slits, and shallow fry in 1 tsp oil with haldi and red chilli until blistered.
In same pan, cook onion-ginger-garlic paste until deep golden brown.
Add tomato puree and spices; cook until oil floats on top.
Add 1 cup water, slide in fried eggs, and simmer for 5-7 minutes. Serve with hot steamed rice.

recipes.title: Masala Bread Omelette
instructions: Whisk 2 eggs with finely chopped onions, green chillies, coriander, salt, and haldi.
Melt butter on a tawa, pour the egg mix evenly.
Dip 2 bread slices into the wet egg, flip them over, and let cook for 2 minutes.
Fold the egg edges over the bread, flip the whole sandwich, and toast until golden and crisp.

recipes.title: Crispy Veggie Besan Chilla
instructions: In a bowl, mix 1 cup besan with water, haldi, ajwain, and salt to form a pourable pancake batter.
Fold in finely chopped onions, tomatoes, chillies, and fresh coriander.
Heat a tawa with a drop of oil. Pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thin circle.
Drizzle oil around edges, flip when bubbles appear, and cook both sides until golden-brown and crisp.

recipes.title: Authentic Kanda Batata Poha
instructions: Rinse thick poha in a colander under running water for 30 seconds; let it rest with haldi and salt.
Heat oil in a pan, fry peanuts until crunchy, and set aside.
In the same oil, crackle rai, curry leaves, and green chillies. Saute diced potatoes and sliced onions until soft.
Gently mix in softened poha, cover for 2 minutes on low steam, and finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice and coriander.

recipes.title: South Indian Veggie Rava Upma
instructions: Dry roast suji (semolina) in a pan on medium flame for 4 minutes until fragrant.
In another pan, heat ghee or oil, add mustard seeds, chana dal, curry leaves, green chillies, and ginger.
Saute onions and any available veggies (carrots/peas) until soft.
Add 2.5 cups water and salt, bring to a rolling boil, then gradually whisk in roasted suji to avoid lumps. Cook covered for 3 minutes.

recipes.title: Punjabi Stuffed Aloo Paratha
instructions: Knead soft dough using whole wheat flour (atta), water, and salt.
Boil, peel, and mash potatoes thoroughly with chopped chillies, coriander, amchur, and salt.
Roll a small dough ball, place potato stuffing inside, seal edges, and roll out gently.
Roast on a hot tawa with generous ghee or butter until both sides have golden-brown spots. Serve with cold dahi.

recipes.title: Gujarati Methi Thepla
instructions: Finely chop fresh methi leaves.
In a mixing bowl, combine atta, 2 tbsp besan, methi, dahi, haldi, red chilli, ajwain, and 1 tsp oil.
Knead into a smooth soft dough without much extra water.
Roll out thin discs and cook on a tawa with oil on high flame for 30 seconds each side to keep them soft.

recipes.title: South Indian Tempered Curd Rice
instructions: Mash cooked soft rice in a bowl. Add fresh dahi, a splash of milk (to prevent souring), and salt.
Heat oil or ghee in a tadka pan. Add rai, hing, ginger, green chillies, and fresh curry leaves.
Pour sizzling tadka over the curd rice.
Mix well and serve chilled or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Street Style Veggie Masala Noodles
instructions: Melt butter in a pan and saute finely chopped onions, chillies, and capsicum.
Add chopped tomatoes and a pinch of haldi and garam masala.
Add 1.5 cups water and the tastemaker spice packet, bringing to a boil.
Break noodle cake into the broth and cook for 2-3 minutes until sauce clings to the noodles.

recipes.title: Bandra Style Cabbage & Capsicum Stir-Fry
instructions: Finely shred fresh cabbage and dice capsicum into matching strips.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan, crackle mustard seeds, jeera, and slit green chillies.
Add chopped tomatoes, haldi, and red chilli powder for 2 minutes.
Toss in shredded cabbage and capsicum on high heat for 3-4 minutes so they stay crisp. Serve hot with rotis.

recipes.title: Gujarati Cabbage & Bell Pepper Sambharo
instructions: Shred cabbage and slice capsicum into thin ribbons.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a kadai, crackle rai (mustard seeds), hing, and green chillies.
Add cabbage and capsicum, haldi and salt. Stir-fry for only 2 minutes—keep it crunchy!
Turn off flame, add a squeeze of fresh lemon juice, and serve as a warm side salad.

recipes.title: Delhi Street Style Fresh Fruit Chaat
instructions: Chop apples, pineapple, strawberries, and grapes into bite-sized cubes in a large bowl.
Sprinkle generous chaat masala, roasted cumin powder, and black salt.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the fruits.
Toss gently and serve chilled.

recipes.title: Crispy Spiced Masala Broccoli
instructions: Cut broccoli into bite-sized florets.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan, add jeera and minced garlic.
Add chopped tomatoes, haldi, and red chilli powder.
Toss in broccoli florets, splash 2 tbsp water, cover and cook for 4-5 minutes until tender-crisp.

recipes.title: Desi Palak Tamatar Ki Sabzi
instructions: Wash and roughly chop fresh leafy spinach (palak).
Heat oil in a kadai, crackle jeera, sliced garlic, and slit green chillies.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and pulpy.
Add chopped spinach and salt; cook for 3-4 minutes until leaves wilt and absorb the tangy tomato flavor.
